assignedReviews.card_evidence: Shadows change because the Sun seems to move across the sky! They are longest in the morning and afternoon, but shortest at midday when the Sun is highest.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the changes in the direction and length of shadows from a shadow stick and use the information to infer why the Sun changes position during a day

copy.en:
Why do shadows change length during the day?

Shadows change because the Sun seems to move across the sky! They are longest in the morning and afternoon, but shortest at midday when the Sun is highest.
copy.tl:
Bakit nagbabago ang haba ng anino sa buong araw?

Nagbabago ang anino dahil sa paggalaw ng Araw sa kalangitan! Pinakamahaba sila sa umaga at hapon, pero pinakamaikli sa tanghali kapag pinakamataas ang Araw.
copy.bis:
Nganong nagbag-o ang gidaba sa anino sa tibuok adlaw?

Nagbag-o ang anino tungod sa paggalaw sa Adlaw sa kalangitan! Pinaka-haba sila sa buntag ug hapon, pero pinaka-mubo sa udto kung pinakataas ang Adlaw.

copy.en: Louis de Broglie proposed that light has a dual nature, meaning it can behave as both a wave and a particle.
copy.tl: Ipinanukala ni Louis de Broglie na may dual nature ang liwanag, ibig sabihin maaari itong kumilos bilang wave at bilang particle.
copy.bis: Gisugyot ni Louis de Broglie nga ang kahayag adunay dual nature, nagpasabot nga mahimo kini molihok isip wave ug isip particle.

copy.en: Loudness is measured in decibels (dB)! A whisper is 30 dB, talking is 60 dB, and a jet is over 120 dB.
copy.tl: Sinusukat ang lakas ng tunog sa decibels (dB)! Ang bulong ay 30 dB, usapan ay 60 dB, at jet ay mahigit 120 dB.
copy.bis: Gisukod ang kakusog sa desibel (dB)! Ang hunghong mga 30 dB, sulti mga 60 dB, ug jet kapin sa 120 dB.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Decomposers recycle matter — atoms and nutrients get used again and again.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the roles of producers, consumers, scavengers, and decomposers in a food web
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions decomposers recycling matter, but it does not describe the roles of producers, consumers, scavengers, and decomposers in a food web. The focus is on energy flow versus matter recycling, not on trophic roles.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: But energy can't be recycled; it slowly turns into heat and disappears, so living things always need fresh sunlight.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use examples of food pyramids to describe the transfer of energy between organisms from one trophic level to another
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses energy transfer in general terms and mentions that energy is not recycled, but it does not use food pyramid examples or describe transfer between trophic levels. It is background for energy flow, not direct instruction for this competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: But energy can't be recycled; it slowly turns into heat and disappears, so living things always need fresh sunlight.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify that energy is something that can cause change including light, sound, and heat energy
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions energy turning into heat, but it does not identify energy as something that can cause change including light, sound, and heat energy. The heat reference is incidental and not used to teach the concept of energy causing change.

copy.en:
Why does the sun's energy never get recycled?

Decomposers recycle matter — atoms and nutrients get used again and again. But energy can't be recycled; it slowly turns into heat and disappears, so living things always need fresh sunlight.
copy.tl:
Bakit hindi na-riricycle ang enerhiya ng araw?

Pinapaikot ng mga decomposer ang materya — paulit-ulit na ginagamit ang mga atomo at sustansya. Pero hindi maaaring i-recycle ang enerhiya; unti-unti itong nawawala bilang init, kaya laging kailangan ang bagong sikat ng araw.
copy.bis:
Ngano nga wala gi-recycle ang enerhiya sa adlaw?

Ang mga decomposer nagpaikot sa materya — balik-balik nga gigamit ang mga atomo ug sustansya. Apan dili marecycle ang enerhiya; anam-anam kining mawala isip kainit, mao nga kanunay gikinahanglan ang bag-ong kahayag sa adlaw.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: In the deep parts of the ocean, it is always dark and very cold because sunlight cannot reach down that far!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify local examples of natural landforms and bodies of water such as mountains, valleys, rivers, and coastlines, and describe how they influence non-living and living components of the environment
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions the ocean, a body of water, but does not identify local examples of landforms/bodies of water or describe how they influence living and non-living components. It only states a fact about deep ocean darkness and coldness due to lack of sunlight.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: In the deep parts of the ocean, it is always dark and very cold because sunlight cannot reach down that far!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe some of the overall characteristics of the Sun, such as its composition, its size, and the main energy it radiates
assignedReviews.reason: The card refers to sunlight not reaching deep ocean, which is tangentially related to the Sun's energy, but it does not describe the Sun's composition, size, or main radiated energy as required by the competency.

copy.en: In the deep parts of the ocean, it is always dark and very cold because sunlight cannot reach down that far!
copy.tl: Sa malalim na bahagi ng dagat, palaging madilim at napakalamig dahil hindi na umaabot doon ang liwanag ng araw!
copy.bis: Sa lawom nga bahin sa dagat, kanunay ngitngit ug bugnaw kaayo tungod kay ang kahayag sa adlaw dili na makaabot ngadto!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Because no sunlight reaches down there!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe sources of light and their use in everyday situations
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions sunlight as a light source but does not describe its use in everyday situations. It focuses on the absence of light in the deep ocean, which is not the competency's focus.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Because no sunlight reaches down there!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe and identify sources and uses of light, sound, and heat energy at school, at home and in the local community
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions sunlight but does not identify sources and uses of light, sound, or heat energy at school, home, or community. It is about deep ocean darkness, not everyday energy sources.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Why is the deepest part of the ocean completely dark?
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify objects, activities, or natural events observed in their local environment that can be explained by science
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes a natural event (deep ocean darkness) but does not identify objects, activities, or natural events in the local environment that can be explained by science. The deep ocean is not a local environment for Grade 3 students.

copy.en:
Why is the deepest part of the ocean completely dark?

Because no sunlight reaches down there! It stays totally dark in the deepest parts of the ocean.
copy.tl:
Bakit patuloy na madilim sa pinakamalalim na bahagi ng karagatan?

Dahil walang sikat ng araw na umaabot doon! Kaya patuloy itong madilim sa pinakamalalim na bahagi.
copy.bis:
Ngano nga kanunay kining ngitngit sa pinakalawom nga bahin sa dagat?

Tungod kay walay sidlak sa adlaw nga moabot didto! Mao nga kanunay kining ngitngit sa kinahiladman.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Deep in the ocean, the water above is so heavy that its pressure could crush an ordinary animal or object from the surface!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify local examples of natural landforms and bodies of water such as mountains, valleys, rivers, and coastlines, and describe how they influence non-living and living components of the environment
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses deep-sea pressure and its crushing effect, which is unrelated to identifying local landforms/bodies of water (mountains, valleys, rivers, coastlines) or describing how they influence living and non-living components. No direct or prerequisite support for the competency.

copy.en:
What can deep-sea pressure do?

Deep in the ocean, the water above is so heavy that its pressure could crush an ordinary animal or object from the surface!
copy.tl:
Ano ang kaya ng presyon sa kailaliman?

Sa kailaliman ng dagat, napakabigat ng tubig sa itaas kaya kayang durugin ng presyon doon ang karaniwang hayop o gamit mula sa ibabaw!
copy.bis:
Unsay mahimo sa presyon sa kadagatan?

Sa kalaliman sa dagat, bug-at kaayo ang tubig sa ibabaw nga ang presyon didto igo nang modugmok sa ordinaryong mananap o butang gikan sa ibabaw!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: the only light down there comes from the animals' own bodies
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use information from secondary sources to describe examples of how some animals have changed to better suit their environment, such as mimicry or camouflage
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions animals producing their own light in the dark deep sea, which hints at an adaptation, but it does not describe how animals have changed to better suit their environment, nor does it use secondary sources or give an example like mimicry or camouflage.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: In the deep sea there is no sunlight at all
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe and identify sources and uses of light, sound, and heat energy at school, at home and in the local community
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about the absence of sunlight and bioluminescence in the deep sea, not about identifying sources and uses of light, sound, or heat energy at school, home, or in the local community.

copy.en: In the deep sea there is no sunlight at all — the only light down there comes from the animals' own bodies.
copy.tl: Sa malalim na bahagi ng dagat ay walang sikat ng araw — ang sariling ilaw ng mga hayop na lang ang liwanag doon.
copy.bis: Sa lawom nga bahin sa dagat walay silaw sa adlaw — ang kaugalingong kahayag sa mga mananap na lang ang kahayag didto.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: some invertebrates grow far bigger than their shallow-water cousins — it's called deep-sea gigantism
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the differences between animals with a backbone (vertebrates) and animals without backbones (invertebrates) by using common local examples of each group
assignedReviews.reason: Invertebrate size in the deep sea is not describing the difference between animals with a backbone and animals without backbones.

copy.en:
Why do some deep-sea creatures grow giant?

In the deep sea, some invertebrates grow far bigger than their shallow-water cousins — it's called deep-sea gigantism. The giant isopod can reach 50 centimeters, while its land relatives are only a few centimeters!
copy.tl:
Bakit malaki ang giant isopod?

Sa malalim na dagat, lumalaki ang invertebrate higit sa kamag-anak sa mababaw na tubig: deep-sea gigantism. Ang giant isopod ay umaabot ng 50 sentimetro, ang kamag-anak sa lupa ay ilang sentimetro lang!
copy.bis:
Nganong dako ang giant isopod?

Sa lawom nga dagat, mudako ang invertebrate og mas dako sa paryenti sa mababaw nga tubig: deep-sea gigantism. Ang giant isopod makaabot og 50 sentimetro, ang paryenti sa yuta pipila lang ka sentimetro!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: sunlight never reaches down there
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe living things, such as animals and plants, as biotic factors and light, water, temperature, and soil type, as abiotic factors in an ecosystem
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions plants and sunlight but does not describe living things as biotic factors or light as an abiotic factor in an ecosystem. It only gives a reason why plants cannot grow in the deep sea, which is background knowledge rather than direct instruction for classifying biotic/abiotic factors.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: sunlight never reaches down there
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify the basic needs of all living things, such as air, food, water, and shelter
assignedReviews.reason: The card implies sunlight is needed for plants, but it does not identify basic needs such as air, food, water, and shelter. The focus is on why plants cannot grow in the deep sea, not on identifying the basic needs of living things.

copy.en:
Why can't plants grow in the deep sea?

No plants can grow in the deep sea because sunlight never reaches down there — so most animals depend on food drifting down from above!
copy.tl:
Bakit walang halamang tumutubo sa malalim na dagat?

Walang halamang tumutubo sa malalim na dagat dahil hindi umaabot doon ang sikat ng araw — kaya umaasa ang mga hayop doon sa pagkaing nahuhulog mula sa itaas!
copy.bis:
Ngano walay tanom nga motubo sa lawom nga dagat?

Walay tanom nga motubo sa lawom nga dagat kay wala moabot didto ang silaw sa adlaw — busa nagsalig ang mga mananap didto sa pagkaon nga nahulog gikan sa ibabaw!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Deep time is the name for the immense spans of geologic history reaching millions and billions of years
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain how the geologic time scale helps to recount the history of the Earth
assignedReviews.reason: The card introduces the concept of deep time as vast geologic history, which is useful background for understanding the geologic time scale, but it does not explain how the geologic time scale helps recount Earth's history.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Deep time is the name for the immense spans of geologic history reaching millions and billions of years
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe how relative and absolute dating techniques are used to determine the subdivisions of geologic time
assignedReviews.reason: The card only mentions immense geologic time spans; it does not describe relative or absolute dating techniques or how they determine subdivisions of geologic time.

copy.en: Deep time is the name for the immense spans of geologic history reaching millions and billions of years — very hard to imagine because it far exceeds human experience!
copy.tl: Ang deep time ay ang tawag sa napakahabang yugto ng kasaysayang heolohiko na umaabot sa milyon at bilyong taon — napakahirap isipin dahil higit na mahaba ito kaysa sa karanasan ng tao!
copy.bis: Ang deep time mao ang ngalan sa hilabihan kataas nga mga yugto sa kasaysayang heolohiko nga moabot sa milyon ug bilyon ka tuig — lisod kaayong hunahunaon kay labaw pa kaayo kini sa kasinatian sa tawo!

assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify the locations of major mountains, faults, volcanos, and ocean trenches using a map of the Philippine Archipelago, and interpret the features in relation to plate tectonics
assignedReviews.reason: The card names an ocean trench and its depth, but it does not use a map of the Philippine Archipelago, identify locations of major Philippine features, or interpret the trench in relation to plate tectonics. copy.bis: Ang pinakalawom nga bahin sa dagat mao ang Challenger Deep sa Mariana Trench, mga 10,935 ka metro o 11 ka kilometro ang giladmon!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The Mariana Trench in the Pacific Ocean is the deepest part

assignedReviews.reason: The card refers to a landform/body of water (ocean trench) but does not identify local examples such as mountains, valleys, rivers, or coastlines, nor describe how they influence living and non-living components. The content is unrelated to the specific local examples and influence described in the competency.

copy.en:
What is the deepest part of our ocean?

The Mariana Trench in the Pacific Ocean is the deepest part, reaching the Challenger Deep at almost 11 kilometers deep!
copy.tl:
Ano ang pinakamalalim na bahagi ng ating karagatan?

Ang Mariana Trench sa Karagatang Pasipiko ang pinakamalalim na bahagi, na umaabot sa Challenger Deep na halos 11 kilometro ang lalim!
copy.bis:
Unsa ang labing lawom nga bahin sa atong kadagatan?

Ang Mariana Trench sa Dagat Pasipiko mao ang labing lawom nga bahin, nga moabot sa Challenger Deep nga halos 11 ka kilometro ang giladmon!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Without trees, soil washes away easily and floods become much worse!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use information from secondary sources to describe the possible effects of human activities, such as deforestation, pollution, and introduction of invasive species, on living things in an ecosystem
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes deforestation and its effects on soil and flooding, but does not describe effects on living things in an ecosystem, which is the focus of the competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Without trees, soil washes away easily
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: demonstrate how erosion transports Earth materials
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions soil washing away, which is erosion, but does not demonstrate how erosion transports Earth materials; it only states a consequence of deforestation.

copy.en: Deforestation means cutting down lots of forest trees at once. Without trees, soil washes away easily and floods become much worse!
copy.tl: Ang deforestation ay ang malawakang pagputol ng mga puno sa gubat. Kapag nawala ang mga puno, mas madaling maguho ang lupa at lumalakas ang baha!
copy.bis: Ang deforestation mao ang dako nga pagputol sa mga kahoy sa lasang. Kon mawala ang mga kahoy, mas dali maguba ang yuta ug mokusog ang baha!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Trees and their roots act like sponges to slow down rainwater
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe the root and shoot system in plants and describe why they are important
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions roots but only as a flood-slowing function; it does not describe the root and shoot system of plants or why these systems are important to the plant itself.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Trees and their roots act like sponges to slow down rainwater
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe the outer parts of plants, such as leaves, roots, and stems and identify their role to get water and nutrients from the soil
assignedReviews.reason: The card refers to roots but does not teach observing outer plant parts or their role in getting water and nutrients from the soil.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Without them, floods on bare hills are much faster and worse!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: demonstrate how erosion transports Earth materials
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions flooding on bare hills but does not demonstrate how erosion transports Earth materials; it only implies a consequence of vegetation loss.

copy.en: Trees and their roots act like sponges to slow down rainwater. Without them, floods on bare hills are much faster and worse!
copy.tl: Ang mga puno at ugat ay nagpapabagal sa tubig-ulan. Kaya kapag kalbo ang bundok, mas mabilis at mas malakas ang baha!
copy.bis: Ang mga kahoy ug gamot nagpahinay sa tubig-ulan. Mao nga kon kalbo ang bukid, mas paspas ug mas grabe ang baha!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The result is soil erosion, flooding, and landslides
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: demonstrate how erosion transports Earth materials
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions soil erosion but does not demonstrate how erosion transports Earth materials. It explains a cause of erosion (loss of tree roots) rather than the transport process itself.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: When forests are cleared, the tree roots that hold soil in place are lost too.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: recognize that there is a need to protect and conserve the environment for living things to survive
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes a harmful effect of deforestation but does not directly teach the need to protect and conserve the environment for living things to survive. It is related background rather than direct instruction for this competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: When forests are cleared, the tree roots that hold soil in place are lost too.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain how interaction between living things and interactions between living and non-living things may bring good or harm to the living things involved
assignedReviews.reason: The card implies an interaction between living things (trees) and non-living things (soil) that can bring harm, but it does not explain how interactions between living and non-living things may bring good or harm. The harm is stated as a result, not explained as an interaction.

copy.en:
Why does cutting down forests cause landslides?

When forests are cleared, the tree roots that hold soil in place are lost too. The result is soil erosion, flooding, and landslides, especially on mountain slopes.
copy.tl:
Bakit nagdudulot ng pagguho ng lupa ang pagkakalbo ng gubat?

Kapag natanggal ang kagubatan, nawawala rin ang mga ugat ng puno na nagtatago sa lupa. Ang resulta ay pagguho ng lupa, pagbaha, at landslide, lalo na sa mga bundok.
copy.bis:
Ngano nakaingon og pagguho sa yuta ang pagpanguha sa kalasangan?

Kon makuha ang kagubatan, mawala usab ang mga gamot sa kahoy nga nagbitik sa yuta. Ang sangputanan mao ang soil erosion, baha, ug landslide, ilabina sa mga kabukiran.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: biodegradable materials are broken down by living things like bacteria
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe and describe the difference between living and non-living things and give examples of each that can be found in the local environment
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses material degradation and mentions living things only as decomposers; it does not teach the difference between living and non-living things or give examples of each.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: biodegradable materials are broken down by living things like bacteria
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify the basic needs of all living things, such as air, food, water, and shelter
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about degradable vs biodegradable materials, not about the basic needs of living things such as air, food, water, and shelter.

copy.en: Degradable materials need help from chemicals, air, sunlight, water, or soil to break down, while biodegradable materials are broken down by living things like bacteria.
copy.tl: Ang mga degradable na materyal ay nangangailangan ng tulong mula sa kemikal, hangin, sikat ng araw, tubig, o lupa para mabulok, habang ang biodegradable na materyal ay binubulok ng mga nabubuhay na bagay tulad ng bacteria.
copy.bis: Ang mga degradable nga materyal nagkinahanglan og tabang gikan sa kemikal, hangin, kahayag sa adlaw, tubig, o yuta aron madugta, samtang ang biodegradable nga materyal gidugta sa mga buhi nga butang sama sa bacteria.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Dehydration — the severe loss of water from the body — is the most dangerous part of cholera and other diarrhea diseases.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify the basic needs of all living things, such as air, food, water, and shelter
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses water loss (dehydration) as a danger in disease, but does not teach students to identify basic needs of living things such as air, food, water, and shelter. It only tangentially relates to water as a need, without supporting the competency's skill of identifying basic needs.

copy.en: Dehydration — the severe loss of water from the body — is the most dangerous part of cholera and other diarrhea diseases.
copy.tl: Ang dehidrasyon — ang labis na pagkawala ng tubig sa katawan — ang pinakadelikadong bahagi ng cholera at iba pang sakit na may pagtatae.
copy.bis: Ang dehidrasyon — ang grabe nga pagkawala sa tubig sa lawas — mao ang labing delikado nga bahin sa cholera ug uban pang sakit nga adunay kalibanga.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: When the body is low on water, we feel thirsty as a warning
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify the basic needs of all living things, such as air, food, water, and shelter
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses thirst as a warning sign of low body water, but it does not identify water (or air, food, shelter) as a basic need of living things. The water mention is incidental to the dehydration warning, not instruction on basic needs.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: When the body is low on water, we feel thirsty as a warning
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe homeostasis as a state of balance among all the body systems in humans that needs to be maintained for survival and proper functioning; its indicators include body temperature, glucose level, and blood pressure
assignedReviews.reason: The card touches on a body response to low water, which is loosely connected to homeostasis, but it does not describe homeostasis as a state of balance among body systems, nor does it address the named indicators (body temperature, glucose level, blood pressure). Thirst is not one of the competency's indicators.

copy.en:
Why do we feel thirsty?

When the body is low on water, we feel thirsty as a warning — it can also cause headaches and weakness, especially in the heat!
copy.tl:
Bakit tayo nauuhaw?

Kapag kulang sa tubig ang katawan, nauuhaw tayo bilang babala — puwede ring sumakit ang ulo at manghina, lalo na kapag mainit!
copy.bis:
Nganong uhawon ta?

Kon kulang sa tubig ang lawas, uhawon ta isip pasidaan — mahimo usab nga sakiton ang ulo ug magluya, ilabi na kon init!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: When you don't drink enough water, you can feel tired, get a headache, or become very thirsty.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify the basic needs of all living things, such as air, food, water, and shelter
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses the effects of dehydration (tiredness, headache, thirst) but does not teach students to identify water as a basic need of living things alongside air, food, and shelter. It only touches on water indirectly and does not support the competency's action of identifying basic needs.

copy.en:
Why do we feel tired without enough water?

When you don't drink enough water, you can feel tired, get a headache, or become very thirsty. Drink up!
copy.tl:
Bakit tayo napapagod kung kulang sa tubig?

Kapag kulang tayo sa tubig, maaari tayong makaramdam ng pagod, sakit ng ulo, o matinding uhaw. Uminom nang sapat!
copy.bis:
Ngano ta maluya kung kulang sa tubig?

Kung kulang kita sa tubig, mahimong mobati kita ug kakapoy, labad sa ulo, o grabe nga kauhaw. Pag-inom og igo!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Your billions of tiny cells are mostly water
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: recognize that some organisms consist of a single cell (unicellular) like in bacteria and some consist of many cells (multicellular) like in a human
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses cell water content and shrinkage during dehydration, but does not address the distinction between unicellular and multicellular organisms, which is the core of G7-L-3.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Your billions of tiny cells are mostly water
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify the basic needs of all living things, such as air, food, water, and shelter
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions water as a component of cells, but does not identify water as a basic need of living things or discuss air, food, water, or shelter as needs. The connection to basic needs is only tangential.

copy.en:
What happens to your cells when you're dehydrated?

Your billions of tiny cells are mostly water — when you're dehydrated, they lose water and shrink a little, so they can't work as well!
copy.tl:
Ano ang nangyayari sa cells mo kapag na-dehydrate ka?

Ang bilyun-bilyong maliliit na cell mo ay karamihan tubig — kapag na-dehydrate ka, nawawalan sila ng tubig at nanguluntoy nang kaunti, kaya hindi maayos ang paggana nila!
copy.bis:
Unsay mahitabo sa imong cells kon ma-dehydrate ka?

Ang binilyon nga gagmay mong cell kasagaran tubig — kon ma-dehydrate ka, mawad-an sila og tubig ug mokuyos gamay, mao nga dili sila makatrabaho og maayo!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: water is still your best defense against dehydration
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify the basic needs of all living things, such as air, food, water, and shelter
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses water as a better drink for hydration compared to sugary sodas and coffee, but it does not teach the competency of identifying the basic needs of all living things (air, food, water, shelter). It only touches on water as a need in a narrow hydration context, without addressing the broader concept of basic needs.

copy.en:
Is soda as good as water for thirst?

Not really! Sugary sodas and coffee aren't as good as plain water — some even make you urinate more, so water is still your best defense against dehydration.
copy.tl:
Kasinghusay ba ng tubig ang softdrinks?

Hindi talaga! Ang matamis na softdrinks at kape ay hindi kasinghusay ng plain na tubig — nagpapadalas pa nga ito ng ihi, kaya tubig pa rin ang pinakamainam laban sa dehydration.
copy.bis:
Sama ba ka maayo ang softdrinks sa tubig?

Dili gyud! Ang tam-is nga softdrinks ug kape dili sama ka maayo sa lunsay nga tubig — nagpadaghan pa hinuon sa ihi, mao nga tubig gihapon ang labing maayo batok sa dehydration.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: eating them helps prevent dehydration
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify the basic needs of all living things, such as air, food, water, and shelter
assignedReviews.reason: The card focuses on water-rich foods preventing dehydration in humans, not on identifying the basic needs of all living things (air, food, water, shelter). It only touches on water as a need for the human body, without addressing the broader set of needs or other living things.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: eating them helps prevent dehydration
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: recognize that water is one of the basic needs of plants and animals
assignedReviews.reason: The competency is about recognizing water as a basic need of plants and animals. The card discusses water intake for humans via food, not plants or animals generally, and does not establish water as a basic need for organisms.

copy.en: Your body doesn't only get water from drinking — juicy fruits and veggies like watermelon, melon, and cucumber are full of water too, and eating them helps prevent dehydration.
copy.tl: Hindi lang sa pag-inom nakakakuha ng tubig ang katawan — puno rin ng tubig ang prutas at gulay tulad ng pakwan, melon, at pipino, kaya ang pagkain ng mga ito ay tumutulong laban sa dehydration.
copy.bis: Dili lang sa pag-inom makakuha ang lawas og tubig — puno usab og tubig ang prutas ug utanon sama sa pakwan, melon, ug pipino, mao nga makatabang ang pagkaon niini batok sa dehydration.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: How much water should a child drink each day?
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify the basic needs of all living things, such as air, food, water, and shelter
assignedReviews.reason: The card gives hydration advice for a child, not instruction on identifying the basic needs of living things (air, food, water, shelter). It assumes water is needed rather than teaching the concept.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: How much water should a child drink each day?
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: recognize that water is one of the basic needs of plants and animals
assignedReviews.reason: The competency is about recognizing water as a basic need of plants and animals. The card only discusses a child's daily water intake and does not address plants or animals generally.

copy.en:
How much water should a child drink each day?

It varies with heat and activity, but a safe rule is to drink often throughout the day — don't wait until you're very thirsty!
copy.tl:
Gaano karaming tubig dapat inumin ng bata?

Nag-iiba ito depende sa init at galaw, pero ang ligtas na gabay ay uminom nang madalas sa buong araw — huwag hintaying mauhaw na mauhaw ka!
copy.bis:
Pila ka tubig angay imnon sa bata?

Magkalahi kini depende sa init ug kalihokan, apan ang luwas nga giya kay moinom kanunay sa tibuok adlaw — ayaw paghulat nga uhaw na kaayo ka!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Dehydration is when your body loses too much water
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify the basic needs of all living things, such as air, food, water, and shelter
assignedReviews.reason: The card explains dehydration as excessive water loss, which is a consequence of lacking water, but it does not teach students to identify water (or air, food, shelter) as a basic need of living things. The competency focuses on recognizing basic needs, not on the effects of water deficiency.

copy.en:
What is dehydration?

Dehydration is when your body loses too much water — often from diarrhea or vomiting.
copy.tl:
Ano ang dehydration?

Ang dehydration ay ang labis na pagkawala ng tubig sa katawan, kadalasan dahil sa pagtatae o pagsusuka.
copy.bis:
Unsa ang dehydration?

Ang dehydration mao ang sobra nga pagkawala sa tubig sa lawas, kasagaran tungod sa kalibanga o pagsuka.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: you still lose water through breathing and urinating — so you still need to drink
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify the basic needs of all living things, such as air, food, water, and shelter
assignedReviews.reason: The card addresses a misconception about dehydration and water loss, not the identification of basic needs of living things (air, food, water, shelter). It assumes water is a need but does not teach students to identify basic needs.

copy.en:
Can you only get dehydrated when it's hot?

No! Even in cold or air-conditioned places, you still lose water through breathing and urinating — so you still need to drink.
copy.tl:
Sa init lang ba tayo nade-dehydrate?

Hindi! Kahit sa malamig o naka-aircon na lugar, patuloy tayong nawawalan ng tubig sa paghinga at pag-ihi, kaya kailangan pa ring uminom.
copy.bis:
Sa init lang ba ka ma-dehydrate?

Dili! Bisan sa bugnaw o naka-aircon nga lugar, padayon ka gihapong mawad-an og tubig pinaagi sa pagginhawa ug pag-ihi, mao nga kinahanglan gihapon ka moinom.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: About two-thirds! Water is in your blood
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify the basic needs of all living things, such as air, food, water, and shelter
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes the proportion of water in the human body and dehydration, but does not teach that water is a basic need of all living things. It is only topically related to water.

copy.en:
How much of your body is actually water?

About two-thirds! Water is in your blood, your cells, even your brain — so losing even a little makes your body feel dehydrated.
copy.tl:
Gaano karaming tubig ang nasa katawan mo?

Halos dalawang-katlo! Nasa dugo, sa mga cell, maging sa utak ang tubig — kaya kahit kaunti lang ang mawala, naramdaman na ito bilang dehydration.
copy.bis:
Unsa kadaghan ang tubig sa imong lawas?

Halos duha-katlo! Anaa sa dugo, sa mga cell, bisan sa utok ang tubig — mao nga bisan gamay ra ang mawala, mabati na kini isip dehydration.

copy.en: A delta is a triangle-shaped piece of land that forms at a river's mouth. The slowing water drops the mud and sand it carries before reaching the sea!
copy.tl: Ang delta ay tatsulok na lupa na nabubuo sa bunganga ng ilog. Ibinababa ng mabagal na agos ang dala nitong putik at buhangin bago lumabas sa dagat!
copy.bis: Ang delta usa ka triyanggulo nga yuta nga maporma sa baba sa suba. Magpahulog ang hinay nga agos sa dala niini nga lapok ug balas una mosulod sa dagat!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: search and destroy mosquito breeding spots
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: recognize that there is a need to protect and conserve the environment for living things to survive
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about dengue prevention, not about protecting or conserving the environment for living things to survive. Destroying breeding spots is a health measure, not an environmental conservation lesson.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: the Philippine health department teaches the 4S
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify issues and concerns in the local community and how they could be addressed by science, such as the treatment of waste
assignedReviews.reason: The card identifies a community health issue (dengue) and a science-based response (4S), but it does not address how the issue could be addressed by science in the sense of treatment of waste or other local environmental concerns. assignedReviews.card_evidence: search and destroy mosquito breeding spots
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain how interaction between living things and interactions between living and non-living things may bring good or harm to the living things involved
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions interactions with the environment (mosquito breeding spots) but does not explain how interactions between living things or living/non-living things bring good or harm. It is a prevention strategy, not an explanation of ecological interactions.

assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe examples and explain how living things depend on one another and on the environment to meet their basic needs
assignedReviews.reason: The card does not explain how living things depend on one another or on the environment to meet basic needs. It is about disease prevention, not about interdependence for basic needs.

copy.en: To fight dengue, the Philippine health department teaches the 4S: search and destroy mosquito breeding spots, protect yourself from bites, seek medical help early, and support fogging when needed.
copy.tl: Para labanan ang dengue, itinuturo ng DOH ang 4S: Search and Destroy ng breeding places ng lamok, Self-Protection mula sa kagat, Seek early consultation, at Support fogging kung kinakailangan.
copy.bis: Aron mapakgang ang dengue, gitudlo sa DOH ang 4S: Search and Destroy sa breeding sites sa lamok, Self-Protection gikan sa kagat, Seek early medical help, ug Support fogging kung gikinahanglan.

assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the physical properties of solid materials, such as hard, shiny, or stretchable
assignedReviews.reason: Cork is a solid material, but the card does not describe physical properties such as hard, shiny, or stretchable. Density is a physical property, but the competency focuses on observable everyday properties, and the card provides no direct support for describing those.

copy.en: The density of cork is about 0.24 grams per cubic centimeter (0.24 g/cm³)!
copy.tl: Ang densidad ng cork ay mga 0.24 gramo bawat sentimetrong kubiko (0.24 g/cm³)!
copy.bis: Ang density sa cork kay mga 0.24 gramo matag kubikong sentimetro (0.24 g/cm³)!

assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe matter as anything that has mass and takes up space
assignedReviews.reason: The card defines density using mass and volume but does not describe matter as anything that has mass and takes up space. It only touches on the concepts of mass and space without teaching the definition of matter itself.

assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions volume but does not instruct on using measuring cylinders or beakers to measure volume, nor does it address units like mL or L. It only uses volume as part of the density formula.

copy.en:
How do we find the density of an object?

Density is the mass in a given space! Just divide the mass by the volume to find it.
copy.tl:
Paano natin malalaman ang densidad ng isang bagay?

Ang densidad ay ang dami ng masa sa isang espasyo! Hatiin lang ang mass sa volume para makuha ito.
copy.bis:
Unsaon nato pagkahibalo sa densidad sa usa ka butang?

Ang densidad mao ang gidaghanon sa masa sa usa ka espasyo! Bahina lang ang mass sa volume aron makuha kini.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Volume is simply the space the object takes up!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe matter as anything that has mass and takes up space
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions volume as space taken up, which touches on matter taking up space, but it does not describe matter as anything that has mass and takes up space. The focus is on the density formula, not the definition of matter.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Volume is simply the space the object takes up!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use measuring cylinders or beakers to measure volume using units, such as milliliters (mL), and liters (L)
assignedReviews.reason: The card defines volume conceptually but does not teach using measuring cylinders or beakers to measure volume in mL or L. No measurement equipment or units are mentioned.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: You can find density by dividing an object's mass by its volume.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify and appropriately use units in simple science activities, such as milligrams (mg), grams (g), kilograms (kg), and degrees centigrade (C)
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions mass and volume but does not identify or use units such as mg, g, kg, or degrees centigrade. It does not support the skill of appropriately using units in science activities.

copy.en: You can find density by dividing an object's mass by its volume. Volume is simply the space the object takes up!
copy.tl: Makikita ang densidad sa pamamagitan ng paghahati ng masa ng bagay sa bolyum nito. Ang bolyum ay ang espasyong kinukuha nito!
copy.bis: Makit-an ang densidad pinaagi sa pagbahin sa gibug-aton sa butang sa iyang gidak-on. Ang gidak-on mao ang espasyo nga gisakop niini!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Density is how much mass is packed into a space!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe matter as anything that has mass and takes up space
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses mass and space in the context of density, but does not describe matter as anything that has mass and takes up space. It uses the concepts without teaching the definition of matter.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Density is how much mass is packed into a space!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use measuring cylinders or beakers to measure volume using units, such as milliliters (mL), and liters (L)
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about density and does not mention measuring cylinders, beakers, volume units, or any measurement procedure. It is unrelated to measuring volume with laboratory equipment.

copy.en:
Ever wonder what density really means?

Density is how much mass is packed into a space! It’s higher when more mass fits in the same volume.
copy.tl:
Napag-isipan mo na ba kung ano ang densidad?

Ang densidad ay kung gaano kasiksik ang masa sa isang espasyo! Mas mataas ito kapag mas maraming masa sa parehong sukat.
copy.bis:
Nakahunahuna na ba ka unsa ang densidad?

Ang densidad mao ang kadasok sa masa sa usa ka luna! Mas taas kini kung mas daghang masa ang sulod sa parehong gidak-on.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: its mass for each amount of space (volume) it takes up
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe matter as anything that has mass and takes up space
assignedReviews.reason: The card defines density using the concepts of mass and volume, but it does not describe matter as anything that has mass and takes up space. It only references these properties in the context of density, so it does not directly support the competency's action.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: its mass for each amount of space (volume) it takes up
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use measuring cylinders or beakers to measure volume using units, such as milliliters (mL), and liters (L)
assignedReviews.reason: The card contains no mention of measuring cylinders, beakers, volume units (mL, L), or any measurement procedure. It only defines density conceptually, so it is unrelated to the competency about using measuring instruments.

copy.en:
What exactly is density?

Density is how tightly packed a material is—its mass for each amount of space (volume) it takes up!
copy.tl:
Ano ba ang density?

Ang density ay kung gaano kasiksik ang isang bagay—ang mass nito sa bawat volume ng espasyong inookupahan nito!
copy.bis:
Unsa man gyud ang density?

Ang density mao ang pagkasiksik sa usa ka materyal—ang mass niini matag gidak-on sa volume nga giokupahan niini!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Density is mass divided by volume (D = M/V)
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe matter as anything that has mass and takes up space
assignedReviews.reason: The card uses the terms mass and volume but does not describe matter as anything that has mass and takes up space. It teaches density, not the definition of matter.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Density is mass divided by volume (D = M/V)
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use measuring cylinders or beakers to measure volume using units, such as milliliters (mL), and liters (L)
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions volume but does not involve measuring cylinders, beakers, or units such as mL and L. It does not support the skill of measuring volume.

copy.en: Density is mass divided by volume (D = M/V). Things with lower density than water float, while higher density makes them sink!
copy.tl: Ang density ay mass hinati sa volume (D = M/V). Ang mga bagay na mas mababa ang density kaysa tubig ay lumulutang, at ang mas mataas ay lumulubog!
copy.bis: Ang density mao ang mass nga gibahin sa volume (D = M/V). Ang mga butang nga mas ubos ang density kaysa tubig naglutaw, ug ang mas taas naglubog!

assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify the properties and uses of metals used by the local community such as iron, gold, silver, and copper
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses a metal (mercury) and its density, but the competency targets properties and uses of local community metals such as iron, gold, silver, and copper. Mercury is not one of these, and no uses are described. The mention of iron is only as a comparison for density, not as a property/use of iron itself.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Mercury is a liquid metal with a high density of 13.6 g/cm3
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the properties of solids, liquids, and gases in terms of shape and volume (solids: definite shape and volume; liquids: no definite shape, definite volume; gases: no definite shape or volume)
assignedReviews.reason: The card states mercury is a liquid metal, but does not describe the properties of liquids in terms of shape and volume (no definite shape, definite volume) nor contrast with solids and gases. It only gives a density value, which is not the competency's focus.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Mercury is a liquid metal with a high density of 13.6 g/cm3
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe matter as anything that has mass and takes up space
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions density, which relates to mass and volume, but does not explicitly describe matter as anything that has mass and takes up space. It does not teach the definition of matter.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Mercury is a liquid metal
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify objects at home and in the classroom as solid, liquid or gas
assignedReviews.reason: The card identifies mercury as a liquid, but does not ask students to identify objects at home or in the classroom as solid, liquid, or gas. It provides a single example without the classification activity or other examples.

copy.en: Mercury is a liquid metal with a high density of 13.6 g/cm3, making it denser than iron! In fact, a piece of iron floats in it, but it's toxic.
copy.tl: Ang mercury ay isang liquid metal na may high density na 13.6 g/cm3, mas siksik kaysa bakal! Kaya lumulutang ang bakal dito, pero ito ay toxic at lason.
copy.bis: Ang mercury usa ka liquid metal nga adunay high density nga 13.6 g/cm3, mas siksik kaysa bakal! Mao nga mulutaw ang bakal dinhi, pero kini toxic ug lason.

assignedReviews.reason: The card teaches the concept of a dependent variable in experiments. It has no connection to safety measures against the Sun's light.

assignedReviews.reason: The card is about experimental measurement, not about the importance of the Sun to living things or class discussion of the Sun.

copy.en: The dependent variable is what you measure or observe to see the result, such as which pancake tastes better.
copy.tl: Ang dependent variable ay ang sinusukat o inoobserbahan mo para makita ang resulta, tulad ng kung aling pancake ang mas masarap.
copy.bis: Ang dependent variable mao ang imong gisukod o giobserbahan aron makita ang resulta, sama sa kung asa nga pancake ang mas lami.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Deposition happens when water slows down and drops the sand and mud it carries.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: demonstrate how erosion transports Earth materials
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes deposition, the settling of transported material, not erosion transporting Earth materials. It does not demonstrate or explain erosion as a transport process, so it only shares the broader topic of Earth materials movement.

copy.en: Deposition happens when water slows down and drops the sand and mud it carries. Where this material piles up, a sandbar can form!
copy.tl: Ang deposition ay nangyayari kapag bumagal ang tubig at ibinaba ang dala-dalang buhangin at putik. Dito nabubuo ang sandbar o tambak ng buhangin!
copy.bis: Ang deposition mahitabo kon mohinay ang tubig ug ibubo ang dala-dalang balas ug lapok. Dinhi maporma ang sandbar o tapok sa balas!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: if one object covers up another one behind it, we know the covering object is closer to us
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: measure and describe changes in the position of people or objects in relation to their original position, such as moving closer, farther, left, or right
assignedReviews.reason: The card explains a static depth cue (occlusion) for judging which object is closer, but the competency requires measuring and describing changes in position relative to an original position (moving closer, farther, left, right). The card does not address movement, measurement, or change over time.

copy.en:
How do we know what's closer with just one eye?

Easy — if one object covers up another one behind it, we know the covering object is closer to us.
copy.tl:
Paano natin alam kung ano ang mas malapit gamit lang ang isang mata?

Madali lang — kapag tinatakpan ng isang bagay ang iba pang bagay sa likod nito, alam nating mas malapit ang tumatakip.
copy.bis:
Unsaon nato pagkahibalo unsay mas duol bisan usa ra ka mata?

Sayon ra — kon gitabonan sa usa ka butang ang lain pa nga butang sa luyo niini, mahibaw-an nato nga mas duol ang nagtabon.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Special plants remove salt from seawater to make fresh drinking water

assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions removing salt from seawater (a separation of a mixture) but does not demonstrate or describe any specific separation technique such as evaporation, filtering, or distillation. assignedReviews.card_evidence: but doing this is very expensive!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain the benefits of each mixture separation technique in preparing useful products
assignedReviews.reason: The card notes that desalination is expensive, which touches on a drawback, but it does not explain the benefits of any specific mixture separation technique in preparing useful products. It does not connect the cost to a named technique or its usefulness.

copy.en:
How do we get fresh drinking water from the salty sea?

Special plants remove salt from seawater to make fresh drinking water, but doing this is very expensive!
copy.tl:
Paano tayo nakakakuha ng tubig-tabang na inumin mula sa maalat na dagat?

May mga pabrika na nag-aalis ng asin sa tubig-dagat para gawing tubig-tabang na pwedeng inumin, ngunit ito ay mahal gawin!
copy.bis:
Unsaon pagkuha og tubig-tab-ang nga mainom gikan sa parat nga dagat?

Naay mga planta nga makatangtang sa asin gikan sa tubig-dagat aron mahimong tubig-tab-ang nga mainom, apan mahal kini buhaton!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: it is very hot during the day but gets very cold at night
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify some of the basic characteristics used to describe the weather, such as air temperature, air pressure, wind speed, wind direction, humidity, rain, and cloud cover
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions temperature variation in a desert, but does not teach identifying basic weather characteristics such as air pressure, wind speed, humidity, etc. It only touches on air temperature as a single fact, not as a characteristic used to describe weather.

Nope! In many deserts, it is very hot during the day but gets very cold at night.

Lagi bang napakainit sa disyerto?

Hindi! Sa maraming disyerto, napakainit sa araw ngunit napakalamig kapag gabi na.
copy.bis:
Lagi bang init kaayo sa desyerto?

Dili! Sa daghang desyerto, init kaayo inig adlaw apan bugnaw kaayo inig gabii.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A desert usually gets less than 25 centimeters of rain in a whole year

How much rain does a desert get?

A desert usually gets less than 25 centimeters of rain in a whole year, making it very dry!
copy.tl:
Gaano karaming ulan ang tumatama sa disyerto?

Karaniwang tumatanggap ang isang disyerto ng wala pang 25 sentimetro ng ulan sa isang taon, kaya napakatuyo nito!
copy.bis:
Pila ka ulan ang makadawat sa desyerto?

Ang desyerto kasagaran makadawat ug ubos sa 25 sentimetro nga ulan sulod sa usa ka tuig, mao nga uga kaayo kini!

copy.en: Many great deserts like the Sahara lie around 30 degrees from the equator, where hot, dried-out air sinks back down, making rain rare!
copy.tl: Maraming malalaking disyerto tulad ng Sahara ay nasa 30 degrees mula sa equator, kung saan bumababa ang natuyong mainit na hangin kaya bihira ang ulan!
copy.bis: Daghang dagkong disyerto sama sa Sahara naa sa 30 degrees gikan sa equator, diin mokunsad ang namala nga init nga hangin maong talagsa ang ulan!

copy.tl: Ang isang carat ay panukat ng bigat ng hiyas, at ito ay katumbas ng 0.2 gramo o 200 milligrams!
copy.bis: Ang usa ka carat mao ang sukod sa gibug-aton sa mutya, ug katumbas kini sa 0.2 gramo o 200 milligrams!

assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify and describe some of the materials formed during volcanic eruptions in the Philippines

How do diamonds reach the surface?

They form deep inside Earth and only reach the surface during a super fast volcanic eruption that carries them up through magma!
copy.tl:
Paano umaabot sa ibabaw ang mga diyamante?

Nabubuo sila nang napakalalim sa Earth at umaabot lang sa ibabaw kapag may sobrang bilis na pagsabog ng bulkan na nagdadala sa kanila sa magma!
copy.bis:
Unsaon pag-abot sa ibabaw ang mga diamante?

Maporma sila lawom kaayo sa Earth ug makaabot lang sa ibabaw kon adunay paspas kaayo nga pagbuto sa bulkan nga modala kanila sa magma!

copy.tl: Ang maliliit na bata ang pinaka-delikadong magka-dehydration kapag nagkasakit, dahil maliit lang ang katawan nila.
copy.bis: Ang gagmay nga mga bata ang labing delikado nga ma-dehydration kon masakit, kay gamay ra ang ilang lawas.

What fuels our big trucks and jeepneys?

Diesel! It is a heavier fraction than gasoline, used to power trucks, jeepneys, and boats.
copy.tl:
Ano ang gatong ng malalaking trak at jeepney?

Diesel! Ito ay isang mas mabigat na bahagi kaysa gasolina, na ginagamit sa mga trak, jeepney, at bangka.
copy.bis:
Unsay sugnod sa mga dagkong trak ug dyip?

Diesel! Kini mas bug-at nga bahin kaysa gasolina, ug gigamit sa mga trak, dyip, ug bangka.

copy.bis: Mahimong lahi ang paghulagway sa lain-laing mga tao sa lokasyon sa parehas nga butang tungod kay lahi ang ilang gipili nga reference point o landmark nga gikumparahan.

copy.bis: Dili managsama ang ulan sa tibuok Pilipinas! Adunay mga dapit nga mouwan bisan sa ting-init tungod sa ilang lahi nga nahimutangan.

Does water dissolve the same amount of every substance?

No! In the same amount of water, much more sugar dissolves than salt because water dissolves different amounts of each substance.

Pareho ba ang natutunaw na dami ng bawat sangkap sa tubig?

Hindi! Sa parehong dami ng tubig, mas maraming asukal ang natutunaw kaysa asin dahil iba-iba ang kayang tunawin ng tubig.
copy.bis:
Parehas ba ang matunaw nga gidaghanon sa matag sangkap sa tubig?

Dili! Sa parehas nga gidaghanon sa tubig, mas daghang asukal ang matunaw kaysa asin tungod kay lahi-lahi ang matunaw sa tubig.

One cell, many cell types?

All your body's cells came from just one fertilized egg — they became different types because different genes switch on in each one!
copy.tl:
Paanong iisang selula naging iba't ibang uri?

Lahat ng selula ng katawan mo ay nagmula sa iisang pinagbuhol na itlog — naging iba't iba sila dahil ibang genes ang gumagana sa bawat isa!
copy.bis:
Giunsa nga usa ka selula nahimong lainlain?

Ang tanang selula sa imong lawas naggikan sa usa ra ka nabungang itlog — nahimo silang lainlain tungod kay lainlaing gene ang naggana sa matag usa!

copy.bis: Kon managsama na ang pagkatag sa mga molekula sa tibuok luna, morag miundang na ang diffusion! Wala nay dapit nga mas daghan o mas gamay.

assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions light being measured by a camera, but it does not describe sources of light or their everyday uses. It focuses on how a camera sensor works, not on identifying light sources or their applications.

How does a digital camera take pictures without film?

It uses a sensor with millions of tiny spots! Each spot measures how much light hits it, and the picture is stored as numbers.
copy.tl:
Paano kumuha ng litrato ang digital camera nang walang pelikula?

May sensor ito na may milyon-milyong maliliit na puntos! Sinusukat ng bawat isa ang dami ng liwanag na tumama, at iniimbak ang larawan bilang mga numero.
copy.bis:
Unsaon pagkuha ug litrato ang digital camera nga walay pelikula?

Adunay sensor kini nga adunay minilyon nga gagmay nga tuldok! Ang matag usa mosukod kung unsa kadaghan ang kahayag nga mitama, ug ang litrato gitipigan isip mga numero.

Why are digital thermometers safer than mercury ones?

Digital thermometers are faster and safer — they have no poisonous liquid and show a digital reading in just a few seconds.
copy.tl:
Bakit mas ligtas ang digital thermometer kaysa sa mercury?

Mas mabilis at mas ligtas ang digital thermometer — walang nakakalason na likido at nagpapakita ng digital na numero sa loob ng ilang segundo.
copy.bis:
Ngano mas luwas ang digital thermometer kaysa sa mercury?

Mas paspas ug mas luwas ang digital thermometer — walay makahilo nga likido ug nagpakita og digital nga numero sa pipila ka segundo.

assignedReviews.reason: The card only distinguishes thermometer types; it does not address planning a scientific investigation, measuring mass, or using a thermometer with appropriate units as required by the competency.

copy.en:
What are the two main types of thermometers?

Some thermometers are digital and show a number on a screen, while others use a rising liquid.
copy.tl:
Ano ang dalawang pangunahing uri ng termometro?

May digital na termometro na nagpapakita ng numero sa screen, at may termometrong gumagamit ng umaakyat na likido.
copy.bis:
Unsa ang duha ka main nga matang sa termometro?

Adunay digital nga termometro nga magpakita og numero sa screen, ug adunay termometro nga mogamit og misaka nga likido.

It controls how much current is allowed through! The less current the dimmer switch lets flow, the dimmer the light becomes.

Kinokontrol nito kung gaano karaming kuryente ang makakadaan! Kapag mas kaunti ang kuryenteng pinadadaloy ng dimmer switch, mas malabo ang ilaw.

Unsaon pag-usab sa dimmer switch sa kahayag sa suga?

Gikontrol niini kung pila ka kuryente ang matugotan moagi! Kung gamay ra ang kuryenteng padaganon sa dimmer switch, mas hanap ang suga.

Hindi pala! Mas malapit ang panahon ng T. rex sa atin ngayon kaysa sa panahon ng Stegosaurus, na nauna ng mahigit 80 milyong taon.

Dungan ba nabuhi ang T. rex ug Stegosaurus?

Unsay tawag sa panahon sa dinosaur?

Ang panahon nga nabuhi ang mga dinosaur gitawag og Mesozoic Era!

Unsa ang buot ipasabot sa extinct?

Kini nagpasabot nga ang tanang hayop niana nga matang namatay ug wala nay buhi — sama sa nahitabo sa mga dinosaur.

How do we know dinosaurs existed?

We know about dinosaurs from fossils -- their bones and traces that turned to stone deep inside the ground.
copy.tl:
Paano natin nalaman na may mga dinosaur?

Alam natin ang tungkol sa mga dinosaur dahil sa fossil -- mga buto at bakas nilang naging bato sa loob ng lupa.
copy.bis:
Unsaon nato pagkahibalo nga naay dinosaur?

Nahibaloan nato ang bahin sa mga dinosaur tungod sa fosil -- ang ilang mga bukog ug timaan nga nahimong bato sulod sa yuta.

copy.en:
How do we know dinosaurs lived in groups?

Fossil footprints show that some dinosaurs traveled together in a herd for protection.
copy.tl:
Paano natin nalaman na may dinosaur na naglalakbay nang magkasama?

Ipinapakita ng mga naprisintang bakas ng paa na ang ilang dinosaur ay naglalakbay nang magkasama bilang kawan para sa proteksyon.
copy.bis:
Giunsa nato pagkahibalo nga adunay dinosaur nga naglakaw nga magkuyog?

Ang mga tunob sa tiil nagpakita nga ang ubang dinosaur nagbiyahe nga magkuyog isip usa ka panon alang sa panalipod.

copy.en:
How do we know dinosaurs were real?

From fossils — ancient bones and traces buried in the ground for a very long time!
copy.tl:
Paano natin nalalaman ang mga dinosaur?

Sa pamamagitan ng fossil — mga lumang buto at bakas na natagpuan sa lupa!
copy.bis:
Giunsa nato mahibaw-an ang mga dinosaur?

Pinaagi sa fosil — karaang bukog ug mga timaan nga nakaplagan ilalom sa yuta!

It means people use the species directly, like cutting bamboo for building huts or making medicine from plant extracts.

Ano ang ibig sabihin ng direct economic value ng isang species?

Ibig sabihin direktang ginagamit ng tao ang species, tulad ng pagputol ng kawayan para sa kubo o paggawa ng gamot mula sa katas ng halaman.
copy.bis:
Unsa ang gipasabot sa direct economic value sa usa ka species?

Nagpasabot nga direktang gigamit sa mga tao ang species, sama sa pagputol sa kawayan para sa payag o paghimo og tambal gikan sa duga sa tanom.

copy.bis: Human sa bagyo o baha sa Pilipinas, importante nga pabukalon o salaon ang tubig! Ang baha kanunay nagdala ug mga kagaw ug hugaw.

copy.bis: Ang go-bag usa ka andam nga bag nga adunay tubig, pagkaon, tambal, flashlight, ug importanteng papeles. Dad-a dayon kon may bagyo, baha, o linog aron luwas!

copy.en: When you cough or sneeze, tiny droplets carrying germs shoot into the air. Cover your mouth and nose with a tissue or your elbow — not your palm — to stop germs from spreading.
copy.tl: Kapag umuubo o bumabahing ka, lumalabas ang maliliit na patak na may germ papunta sa hangin. Takpan ang bibig at ilong gamit ang tisyu o siko — huwag ang palad — para hindi kumalat ang germ.
copy.bis: Kung mag-ubo o mobahin ka, mogawas ang gagmay nga tinulo nga adunay germ padulong sa hangin. Taboni ang baba ug ilong gamit ang tisyu o siko — dili ang palad — aron dili mokatag ang germ.

assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe in simple terms how the following human body systems work: muscular, skeletal, digestive, circulatory, and respiratory
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses immunity and resistance, not the muscular, skeletal, digestive, circulatory, or respiratory systems. No direct or prerequisite support for describing how any of these body systems work.

copy.en:
Why does only one person get sick?

Two people can meet the same germ, but only one gets sick — because their immune systems differ in strength. Enough sleep and good food make resistance stronger.
copy.tl:
Bakit isa lang ang nagkasakit sa dalawa?

Dalawang tao pwedeng malapitan ng parehong germ, pero isa lang ang magkasakit — dahil iba't iba ang lakas ng kanilang immune system. Ang sapat na tulog at masustansyang pagkain ay nagpapalakas ng resistensya.
copy.bis:
Nganong usa ra ang nagmasakit sa duha?

Duha ka tawo mahimong maabtan sa samang germ, apan usa ra ang mamasakit — kay lahi-lahi ang kusog sa ilang immune system. Ang igo nga tulog ug masustansya nga pagkaon nagpakusog sa resistensya.

copy.en: Heating, stirring, and crushing a solute into smaller pieces help it dissolve faster in a solvent.
copy.tl: Ang pag-init, paghalo, at pagdurog sa solute sa mas maliliit na piraso ay nakakatulong para mas mabilis itong matunaw sa solvent.
copy.bis: Ang pagpainit, pagpalihok, ug pagdugmok sa solute ngadto sa gagmay nga mga piraso makatabang aron mas paspas kini matunaw sa solvent.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: It has far too much dissolved salt.

assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions dissolved salt in seawater, which is an example of a solution (uniform mixture), but it does not describe the mixture itself or its classification. copy.en:
Can I drink seawater if it looks clear?

No! It has far too much dissolved salt. Too much salt is bad for the body and makes you even thirstier instead of quenching your thirst.
copy.tl:
Pwede ba inumin ang tubig-dagat kahit malinaw?

Hindi! Sobrang dami ng natunaw na asin dito. Masama ito sa katawan at nakakauhaw pa sa halip na makawala ng uhaw.
copy.bis:
Pwede ba imnon ang tubig-dagat bisan tin-aw?

Dili! Sobra ra kadaghan ang natunaw nga asin niini. Daotan sa lawas ug makapauhaw pa imbis nga mopawala sa kauhaw.

copy.en: Water can't dissolve salt forever! When there's too much salt, the extra won't dissolve and settles at the bottom — the water is saturated.
copy.tl: Hindi kayang tunawin ng tubig ang asin nang walang katapusan! Kapag sobra na, hindi na matutunaw ang extra at lulubog sa ilalim — saturated na ang tubig.
copy.bis: Dili makatunaw ang tubig sa asin nga walay katapusan! Kon sobra na, dili na matunaw ang extra ug molunod sa ilawom — saturated na ang tubig.

What does a jeepney's distance-time graph look like on its route?

It looks like a staircase! The line rises when it moves, goes flat when it stops for passengers, then rises again—a classic rise-flat-rise trip in the Philippines!

Ano ang itsura ng distance-time graph ng jeepney sa ruta nito?

Parang hagdan! Umaakyat ang linya pag-usad, patag paghinto para sa pasahero, tapos umaakyat ulit—isang pamilyar na rise-flat-rise na biyahe sa Pilipinas!

Unsay dagway sa distance-time graph sa jeepney sa iyang ruta?

Murag hagdanan! Mosaka ang linya kung molihok, mopatag kung mohunong para sa pasahero, unya mosaka pag-usab—usa ka pamilyar nga saka-patag-saka nga biyahe sa Pilipinas!

Can a perfectly vertical line exist on a distance-time graph?

No! That would mean jumping a distance in zero time. That means infinite speed, which is totally impossible in real life!
copy.tl:
Puwedeng magkaroon ng perpektong patindig na linya sa distance-time graph?

Hindi! Ibig sabihin niyon ay lumayo nang walang oras na lumipas. Walang-hangganang bilis iyon, na imposible sa totoong buhay!

Mahimong mahimo ang hingpit nga patindog nga linya sa distance-time graph?

Dili! Nagpasabot kini nga milayo nga walay oras nga milabay. Walay kinutoban nga katulin kini, nga imposible sa tinuod nga kinabuhi!

copy.en:
Why does a distance-time graph usually start at the origin?

Because at the very start, zero time has passed and the object hasn't traveled anywhere yet! The clock has just begun ticking.
copy.tl:
Bakit karaniwang nagsisimula ang distance-time graph sa origin?

Dahil sa simula pa lang, zero oras pa lang at wala pang nilalakbay ang bagay! Sisimula pa lang ng takda ng oras.
copy.bis:
Ngano nga kasagaran magsugod ang distance-time graph sa origin?

Tungod kay sa sinugdanan pa lang, zero oras pa lang ug wala pa nagalakaw ang butang! Bag-o pa lang nagsugod ang orasan.

How to spot the faster vehicle on a graph?

On a distance-time graph, the steeper line belongs to the faster vehicle! If a jeepney's line is steeper than a tricycle's, the jeepney is faster—no numbers needed!
copy.tl:
Paano malalaman kung alin ang mas mabilis sa graph?

Sa distance-time graph, ang mas matarik na linya ay sa mas mabilis na sasakyan! Kung mas matarik ang linya ng jeepney kaysa tricycle, mas mabilis ang jeepney!
copy.bis:
Unsaon pagkahibalo kung hain ang mas paspas sa graph?

Sa distance-time graph, ang mas tarik nga linya iya sa mas paspas nga sakyanan! Kung mas tarik ang linya sa jeepney kay sa tricycle, mas paspas ang jeepney!

How do you find the exact speed at one instant on a curved line?

Draw a straight line, called a tangent, that just touches the curve at that exact point! The slope of that tangent is the speed at that moment.
copy.tl:
Paano malalaman ang eksaktong bilis sa isang sandali sa kurbadong linya?

Gumuhit ng tuwid na linya (tangent) na dumidikit lang sa kurba sa puntong iyon! Ang slope ng tangent na iyon ang bilis sa sandaling iyon.

Unsaon pagmahibalo sa eksaktong katulin sa usa ka gutlo sa kurbado nga linya?

Pagdrowing og tul-id nga linya (tangent) nga modikit lang sa kurba niana nga punto! Ang slope niana nga tangent mao ang katulin niana nga higayon.

Why can't a graph line go left?

On a distance-time graph, time on the horizontal axis always moves forward! It never goes back, so lines can never go left—time always flows right.
copy.tl:
Bakit hindi pwedeng pumunta sa kaliwa ang linya sa graph?

Sa distance-time graph, ang oras sa horizontal axis ay palaging gumagalaw pasulong! Hindi ito bumabalik, kaya hindi pwedeng pumunta sa kaliwa ang linya—laging sa kanan.
copy.bis:
Ngano nga dili pwede mobalik sa wala ang linya sa graph?

Sa distance-time graph, ang oras sa horizontal axis kanunay molihok pasulong! Dili kini mobalik, mao nga dili pwede mobalik sa wala ang linya—kanunay sa tuo.

We measure distance in units such as meters and kilometers!
